result:
If I could change one thing, I'd make curiosity and intellectual honesty the strongest human drives — stronger than status, comfort, or tribal belonging.

Everything else is downstream of that. Most of the world's stupidity, cruelty, and self-sabotage comes from people being more interested in protecting their existing beliefs, feelings, or group identity than in figuring out what's actually true. If that incentive structure flipped, a lot of other problems would start solving themselves. 

Not because everyone would suddenly be "good," but because they'd be less interested in lying to themselves and each other.

This is achieved conceptually by re-engineering incentive structures: reward systems are realigned so that agents who pursue verifiable models of reality receive higher status, resources, and influence, while agents who rely on un 1) falsifiable narratives or tribal loyalty receive lower status.
